title: Subtree of Another Tree
statement: Return true if tree subRoot is structurally identical to a subtree of root, including node values.
explanation: At every node of root, test whether the two trees are identical; otherwise search the left and right subtrees.

title: Distribute Candies
approach: Distinct types versus half the candies
statement: A sister receives exactly half of an even-sized candy array. Return the maximum number of distinct candy types she can receive.
explanation: The answer is the smaller of the number of distinct types and half the total candy count.

title: Shortest Unsorted Continuous Subarray
approach: Find disorder boundaries and extend by min/max
statement: Return the length of the shortest continuous subarray that, if sorted, makes the entire array sorted.
explanation: Find the first and last descending adjacent pairs, compute the minimum and maximum within that range, then extend the boundaries while outside values violate the range.

title: Delete Operation for Two Strings
statement: Return the minimum number of character deletions needed to make two strings equal.
explanation: Keep a longest common subsequence; every other character must be deleted from one of the two strings.

title: N-ary Tree Preorder Traversal
approach: Root then children from left to right
statement: Return the preorder traversal of an N-ary tree: visit a node before its children, processing children from left to right.
explanation: Visit the current node, then recursively traverse each child in list order.
example: root with children 3, 2, 4 and node 3 having children 5, 6 -> [1,3,5,6,2,4]

title: N-ary Tree Postorder Traversal
statement: Return the postorder traversal of an N-ary tree: traverse each child from left to right before visiting the node.
explanation: Recursively visit each child in list order and append the current node after all children.
example: root with children 3, 2, 4 and node 3 having children 5, 6 -> [5,6,3,2,4,1]

title: Longest Harmonious Subsequence
statement: Return the length of the longest subsequence whose maximum and minimum values differ by exactly one.
explanation: Count frequencies and maximize count[x] + count[x+1] over values with both neighbors present.

title: Range Addition II
statement: Starting with an m by n zero matrix, each operation increments every cell in a top-left rectangle. Return how many cells have the maximum value after all operations.
explanation: Cells in the overlap of every operation's rectangle receive all increments; the overlap dimensions are the minimum operation row and column bounds.

title: Minimum Index Sum of Two Lists
approach: Map first-list indices and minimize index sum
statement: Return all common strings from two lists whose sum of indices is minimal.
explanation: Store each first-list index, scan the second list, and keep all matches with the smallest index sum.
example: list1=["Shogun","Tapioca Express","Burger King"], list2=["Piatti","The Grill at Torrey Pines","Shogun"] -> ["Shogun"]

title: Can Place Flowers
approach: Greedily plant where both neighbors are empty
statement: Determine whether n new flowers can be planted in a flowerbed without placing flowers in adjacent plots.
explanation: Scan left to right and plant in an empty plot only when its immediate neighbors, if present, are empty.
